A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ParallelComp. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench and InfiniteBench evaluations, NarrativeQA perplexity measurements, attention-bias ablations and throughput experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds experiments with long-context models, additional comparison methods and baseline hyperparameter sensitivity tests.

M1.justification: The core pipeline remains chunked parallel attention, self-information-based chunk selection, low/high-attention token eviction and global attention. Explicit head indices and expanded score descriptions do not establish a new component; v1 already states that its implementation uses multi-head attention.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same LongBench and InfiniteBench tasks and use NarrativeQA for perplexity and throughput. The added model and baseline evaluations reuse this coverage rather than introducing new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with adaptive parallel encoding (APE), StarAttention and ChatQA-2, including ChatQA-2 with RAG on LongBench (Tables 9–12). Tables 4–5 also compare against unmodified Llama3.1 and Qwen2.5. These substantially extend the comparator set beyond v1's retained baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix C changes Llama3's compressed cache from 2000 to 4000 tokens, sink/recency regions from 200 to 100 tokens, and retained PRe chunks from three to one. New evaluations introduce Llama3.1/Qwen2.5, a 24K cache budget, 6K positional reuse and prompt-token controls. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 12 adds a focused sensitivity study varying APE temperature/scaling and StarAttention chunk size. The existing InfiniteBench layer/token-eviction ablation is revised (v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 6), while the LongBench appendix ablation and attention visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added probabilistic assumptions in Appendix A concern theoretical proofs, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises Llama3 results, including Ours AVG from 45.37 to 44.93 and Ours-calibration from 45.74 to 45.21. Table 2 changes Llama2 Ours-calibration AVG from 52.71 to 51.27, and numerous InfiniteBench ablation entries change. v2 also adds substantial model/baseline results; Table 12 reports tuned APE at 38.47 versus ParallelComp at 38.15. Changed settings preclude interpreting all revisions as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A expands the earlier local-sparsity argument into six theorems covering local/global exponential decay, tail bounds and sparsity, introducing distance-dependent dot-product and sub-Gaussian assumptions. Theorem 3.1 also reverses its stated threshold trend from increasing to decreasing with chunk width. These are substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the 4K-to-128K, preserved-perplexity framing with 8K-to-128K extrapolation and negligible performance loss, emphasizing memory bottlenecks. The 91.17%-of-GPT-4 and throughput claims remain. The conclusion still states 4K-to-128K, leaving the revised scope inconsistently expressed.

C2.justification: Section 4 now qualifies whether reducing attention bias improves task performance. The ablation discussion changes the implicated recency-bias layers and adds a role for deep middle-bias tokens in reading comprehension. New discussions interpret positional reuse in long-context models and attribute comparator weaknesses to retrieval instability or input truncation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release link, query-chunk perplexity clarification, Figure 1 model/head identification and baseline configuration details. Appendix C revises hardware from an 80GB A100 to eight 64GB MI210 GPUs and removes the explicit 23-chunk total and 0.1/0.3 threshold settings. These materially change reproducibility information, although hardware descriptions remain inconsistent.

R1.justification: The training-free extrapolation positioning remains, with focused additions discussing APE, StarAttention, ChatQA-2 and KV-cache compression research. Chunk-selection attribution changes from Ye et al. to Li et al. and Jiang et al.; the LongLoRA citation is removed. These extend rather than replace the existing research framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with further method-language revisions and changed terminology. v2 adds a dedicated long-context-model subsection and Future Work, reorganizes Appendix A into five subsections, and introduces Appendix D. The narrative revision extends beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables for model comparisons, RAG comparisons and baseline sensitivity analyses. Existing tables are rearranged, average columns in Tables 1–2 gain colored highlighting, and figures are repositioned. Figures 1–6 retain their underlying visual content, with an expanded Figure 1 caption.

improvement.justification: The added comparisons, sensitivity tests and code link improve empirical context and reproducibility information. However, new Table 5's Llama3.1 averages do not match its displayed task values, and unchanged throughput measurements are reassigned to 64GB MI210 hardware while still reporting 79,742MB peak memory. Expanded Theorem A.3 also claims w-o(w) entries above a fixed threshold, conflicting with normalized attention. These benefits and reliability problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
